newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus tells U.S. to show more respect.
newsitem.headline: Belarus tells U.S. to show more respect.

text.p: A spokesman for Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko's Security Council, reacting to a protest by the U.S. Embassy on Monday over the expulsion of its first secretary, demanded that Americans show more respect.
"This is not normal when foreign citizens interfere in the internal affairs of another state," said Vasily Baranov, the Council's press secretary.
"Despite its problems Belarus is a sovereign state and not a hallway. Bigger countries should respect its sovereignty," he added.
Belarus ordered U.S. diplomat Serzh Alexandrov to leave within 24 hours after he was arrested at an opposition rally on Sunday and accused of spying for the Central Intelligence Agency.
The U.S. Embassy responded by accusing Minsk of "arbitrary and unjustified" action.
Another U.S. citizen, the local executive director for the Soros Foundation, was barred earlier this month from returning to the ex-Soviet nation and accused of backing Lukashenko's opposition.
Both men were present at one of a series of recent rallies against Lukashenko. The U.S. embassy said Alexandrov was carrying out normal diplomatic duties by observing a protest.
Baranov said the situation in Belarus was being wrongly interpreted and accused the United States of encouraging the opposition, which it said did not reflect the will of most Belarussians.
"The United States encourages people, in the knowledge that they are going against the will of the majority," Baranov said.
"When in Rome, do as the Romans do. For example I cannot imagine myself taking part in an action aimed at overthrowing President (Bill) Clinton," he added.
